ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a composite figure; the main body looks like a rectangle, with an inward concave semicircular notch on the left side and a pointed triangle connected on the right side. The upper horizontal side is labeled 13 m, the left dashed vertical segment is labeled 10 m, and this dashed line corresponds to the diameter of the semicircular notch. The two slanted sides of the right triangle have the same tick marks, and one of them is labeled 9 m, so both slanted sides are 9 m. Reasoning: According to the method, view the figure as a 13 m × 10 m rectangle, plus the right isosceles triangle, minus the left semicircular notch. The area of the rectangle is 13 × 10 = 130. The semicircle diameter is 10 m, so the radius is 5 m, and the semicircle area is (1/2)π(5^2) = 12.5π. The base of the right isosceles triangle equals the rectangle height 10 m, and the two legs are 9 m; the altitude bisects the base into 5 m and 5 m, so the triangle height is sqrt(9^2 - 5^2) = sqrt(56). The triangle area is (1/2) × 10 × sqrt(56) = 5sqrt(56). Total area = 130 + 5sqrt(56) - 12.5π ≈ 128.1467, rounded to the nearest tenth is 128.1.

method.method_draft: Read the figure as a 13 m by 10 m rectangle with a concave semicircular cutout on the left and an isosceles triangular point attached on the right. From the image, the dashed vertical segment is the semicircle’s diameter, 10 m, so the semicircle radius is 5 m. The two slanted sides of the right triangle are marked congruent, and one is labeled 9 m, so both are 9 m; its base is the rectangle height, 10 m. Compute total area as rectangle area plus triangle area minus semicircle area: 13*10 + (1/2)*10*sqrt(9^2-5^2) - (1/2)*pi*5^2, then round to the nearest tenth.

method.method_draft: Read the outer straight-edged part as a rectangle of width 13 m and height 10 m plus an isosceles triangle whose equal sides are 9 m and whose third side is the 10 m vertical segment between the horizontal edges. Find the polygonal area first: rectangle area 13*10, and triangle area by Heron’s formula with sides 9, 9, and 10, using semiperimeter 14, so triangle area is sqrt(14(14-9)(14-9)(14-10)). Then read the left curved boundary as a semicircle with diameter 10 m, hence radius 5 m, and subtract its area, (1/2)pi*5^2. Round the resulting area to the nearest tenth.
